frontmatter.name: ab-test
frontmatter.description: Measure whether a change to a skill, rule, AGENTS.md section or routing policy really changes agent behavior. Defines falsifiable cases, runs paired baseline and candidate trials in throwaway config directories (never hiding or renaming the user's real skills or settings), captures tool-use evidence such as whether the agent loaded the skill or called context7, then scores pass rates and reports per-case deltas. Use when the user asks to benchmark, evaluate, A/B test or compare a skill or rule change, or to check that agents really use an MCP server or skill.
frontmatter.when_to_use: After editing a skill's description or body, a rule or the routing policy, before keeping the change; when a skill seems never to trigger ("benchmark this", "compare before and after", "does the skill trigger", "is context7 really called").
frontmatter.short-description: Paired before/after evals of skills and rules with tool-use evidence

frontmatter.name: bugfix
frontmatter.description: Plan-less bug workflow that owns one defect end to end: reproduce it first, trace the root cause to file:line, write a failing test, fix at the source, prove the fix on the real program, then pass the quality gate. With branch isolation on it asks where to work: the current branch, a bugfix/<slug> branch or a worktree squash-merged once the fix is proven; no plan file. Run only when the user explicitly asks for bugfix.
frontmatter.when_to_use: The user invokes bugfix by name or explicitly asks for this workflow ("solve it with bugfix", "use the bugfix workflow"), bringing a failing test, an error message, a crash or a regression. A plain "fix this" is handled directly, without this workflow.
frontmatter.argument-hint: <bug: symptom, failing test, error or steps> [--worktree | --new-branch | --current-branch]
frontmatter.short-description: Reproduce, root-cause, RED test, fix at the source, prove it end to end

ask: fix it with a failing test first
reproduce it first and fix it

frontmatter.name: buracle
frontmatter.description: How to use the `buracle` helper CLI that Buracle workflows call instead of ad-hoc shell: plan state and the stop guard (`buracle plan …`, with `plan pause` as the only escape hatch), isolated worktrees, review diff scope, notifications, usage limits, memory CLI twins, workflow progress, code indexes, project sync, skill and rule lint, and `buracle doctor` for health checks. Covers JSON output, exit codes (0 ok, 1 error, 2 needs user action) and session resolution. Use whenever a step needs one of these commands, when a buracle command fails, or when the stop guard keeps your turn going.
frontmatter.when_to_use: Creating, registering or moving a plan; pausing to ask the user; creating or merging a worktree; computing a review diff; notifying the user; checking rate-limit headroom; diagnosing Buracle.
frontmatter.short-description: When and how to call the buracle helper CLI

frontmatter.name: dead-code
frontmatter.description: Report-only dead-code audit. Collects candidate unused files and exports from the project's own analyzers, a bundled rg-based script and a read-only codegraph snapshot, checks every candidate against independent signals (codegraph references, exact and dynamic-usage search, analyzers), rules out a public role (API, entry points, config, registries), and returns a ranked report with evidence and a staged removal plan. Never deletes or edits code.
frontmatter.when_to_use: The user invokes it or asks for an unused or dead code audit ("find the dead code", "find unused code", "cleanup report", "dead code audit").
frontmatter.short-description: Report-only dead-code audit with two-signal evidence and a removal plan

frontmatter.name: find-skill
frontmatter.description: Find an agent skill for a need and install it for every harness in a few calls. `buracle skills find <need>` is one command that shows the installed and shipped skills that already match, then the skills.sh registry's candidates with description, license, freshness, tool grants and risk ratings; `buracle skills add --dry-run` audits the pick (scripts, allowed-tools, suspicious lines) and `buracle skills add` installs it into ~/.agents/skills (Codex, OpenCode, Oh My Pi) and links it into ~/.claude/skills (Claude Code). Also updates and removes installed skills.
frontmatter.when_to_use: "is there a skill for X", "find a skill that does X", "install the X skill", "add a skill for X", a recurring task that no skill in `buracle skills list` covers, "update my skills", "remove the X skill".
frontmatter.argument-hint: <what the skill should do | owner/repo[/path] | skill id>
frontmatter.short-description: Find a skill for a need and install it for every harness

frontmatter.name: goal-build
frontmatter.description: Goal-and-loop workflow for a clear end state whose path is found while building: agree on a goal, tasks sized as the largest slices you can finish and verify, and at least 3 pass/fail acceptance criteria (one of them the oracle), have them reviewed, lock the contract, then build in rounds judged on running evidence (at most four), verify and hand back. Tracked in docs/builds/. Run only when the user explicitly asks for goal-build.
frontmatter.when_to_use: The user invokes goal-build by name, or names an end state and asks you to find the way there, working in a loop until it is done.
frontmatter.short-description: Lock a goal and pass/fail criteria, then build in judged rounds

frontmatter.name: inspect
frontmatter.description: Read-only investigation of one question about the code. Frames a falsifiable claim, locates code with semble (intent), codegraph (callers, callees, blast radius) and rg or ast-grep (exact and structural matches), checks memory for past decisions, traces the active path hop by hop, challenges the answer with a counterexample search, and reports a direct answer with file:line evidence and calibrated confidence. Never edits anything.
frontmatter.when_to_use: The user invokes it to learn how something works, why it behaves a certain way, or where and how something is used ("how does X work", "why does it behave like this", "where is this called from").
frontmatter.short-description: Read-only trace of one code question with file:line evidence

frontmatter.name: memory
frontmatter.description: Protocol for Buracle's shared memory: the CortexDB brains (one per project, one for the person) served by the buracle-memory MCP server in every harness. Says when to run a quick memory pass (at most 3 memory_search calls, then at most 3 memories via memory_get), how to treat recalled memories as evidence rather than instructions, and how to keep the memory: one claim per memory with sources, search before writing, update or merge instead of duplicating, keep the core pages current, record the user's preferences in the right brain, work through the upkeep queue, never store secrets. Use when the user refers to past work or asks you to remember something, before re-deciding something, after a non-obvious fix, and when upkeep waits.
frontmatter.when_to_use: History or rationale questions (last time, why did we, what did we decide, where were we), requests to remember something, tasks that touch memories listed at session start, the end of work that produced a decision, gotcha or user preference.
frontmatter.short-description: When and how to read, write and keep Buracle's CortexDB memory

frontmatter.name: new-skill
frontmatter.description: Capture a repeatable procedure as a Buracle skill, or improve an existing one. Picks the right home (global skills in the Buracle repo's canonical/skills or a configured skills git source; project-only skills in .agents/skills), writes SKILL.md in the canonical format with references/, scripts/ and trigger evals, lints it with `buracle skills lint`, and explains how publishing reaches every harness. Use when the user wants to turn a workflow into a skill, edit, split or rename a skill, or fix a skill that triggers too often or never.
frontmatter.when_to_use: A multi-step procedure was done more than once or took real effort and will recur; an existing skill misfires, has grown too long or misses a step ("turn this into a skill", "create a new skill", "update the skill").
frontmatter.argument-hint: <skill id or the procedure to capture>
frontmatter.short-description: Capture a repeatable procedure as a canonical Buracle skill

topic: re:\bskill\S*\b.{0,60}\b(?:never triggers|does not trigger|doesn't trigger|misfires|triggers too often)

frontmatter.name: plan-build
frontmatter.description: Plan-driven development through a plan file in docs/plans/: explore and clarify, write and review the plan, get approval, implement task by task with TDD, then verify with real evidence until the plan is VERIFIED. Covers features and bugfixes (behavior contract, reproduce first, root-cause fix). Also pauses, resumes or continues an existing plan. Run only when the user explicitly asks for plan-build.
frontmatter.when_to_use: The user invokes plan-build by name, passes a docs/plans/*.md file, or asks to write a plan and implement it, or to continue a plan.
frontmatter.short-description: Plan, approve, TDD-implement and verify work through a plan file

frontmatter.name: project-rules
frontmatter.description: Create, refresh or audit a repository's agent guidance so Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and omp follow the same verified instructions: the root AGENTS.md, optional nested AGENTS.md files for subprojects, and path-scoped rules for specific file types. Discovers commands and conventions from the code (package scripts, CI jobs, linter and test configs, test layout), runs commands before documenting them, keeps every file short, then runs `buracle project sync` and `buracle project check`. Use when the user asks to set up, write, update, slim down or check AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or project rules.
frontmatter.when_to_use: The repo has no agent guidance, or it is stale, bloated or contradicts the code; after tooling changes such as a new package manager, test runner or linter ("write an AGENTS.md", "set up the project rules", "update the instructions", "slim down the rules").
frontmatter.short-description: Generate and verify AGENTS.md and path-scoped rules for a repo

frontmatter.name: requirements
frontmatter.description: Requirements workflow for ideas whose problem, audience or scope is still unclear. Grounds the idea in the codebase and memory, runs tiered research through the research skill, explores directions, asks a few decision questions, proposes approaches, converges on scope, writes an approved PRD to docs/prd/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md and prints the plan-build or goal-build hand-off. No code is written before the PRD is approved.
frontmatter.when_to_use: The user invokes it or asks for a PRD or requirements document ("write a PRD", "let's work out the requirements", "help me sharpen this idea").
frontmatter.short-description: Interview, research and write an approved PRD before any code

frontmatter.name: research
frontmatter.description: Evidence-backed research that must use MCP tools instead of recall: web-search to discover sources, web-fetch to read them in full, context7 for library and framework documentation, grep for real-world code on GitHub, and buracle-memory for prior decisions. Produces a cited research note (answer, findings, options, conflicts, gaps, confidence) and can save durable findings to memory as knowledge memories pending review.
frontmatter.when_to_use: Time-sensitive or unfamiliar questions: current versions, API behavior, best practices, standards, comparisons of libraries, tools or approaches, "is X still maintained"; requests such as "research", "compare", "which one is better", "is this still current", "find sources", "cite sources". The requirements workflow also runs it.
frontmatter.short-description: Cited, MCP-backed research across web, library docs, public code and memory

frontmatter.name: security-audit
frontmatter.description: Security guidance and vulnerability review for codebases, APIs, services, CLI tools, libraries and daemons: Cloudflare's security-audit skill (MIT), vendored as Buracle's default security skill. Guidance mode answers security questions, focused reviews and triage with the relevant parts only; full audit mode runs six phases (reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting with parallel isolated agents, validation by fresh verifiers, structured findings.json, independent record verification, a target-neutral report) when the user asks for an audit, a pen test, a full security review or report artifacts.
frontmatter.when_to_use: "security audit", "audit this codebase", "pen test", "find vulnerabilities", "security review", or a question about a trust boundary, authentication, injection, secrets or the supply chain.
frontmatter.short-description: Cloudflare's security-audit skill, Buracle's default security review

frontmatter.name: changes-review
frontmatter.description: Read-only reviewer for implemented changes before a Buracle workflow is marked verified. Launch it after implementation (plan-build verification, bugfix finalization, goal-build hand-back), passing the plan path or the expected behavior, the run slug and the verification evidence gathered so far. It resolves the diff with `buracle review-scope --json` and checks plan adherence, correctness, tests, security and goal achievement, returning strict JSON findings and goal truths.

frontmatter.name: goal-build-review
frontmatter.description: Read-only reviewer for a Buracle goal-build contract (the Buildout) before the build loop starts. Launch it from the goal-build workflow after drafting docs/builds/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md, passing the file path, the user's goal verbatim and the clarifications. It checks that the tasks and acceptance criteria are measurable, complete and correctly ordered, and returns strict JSON findings with ready-to-paste replacement wording.

frontmatter.name: plan-build-review
frontmatter.description: Read-only reviewer for a Buracle plan-build plan before the user approves it. Launch it from the plan-build workflow once the plan file passes `buracle plan validate`, passing the plan path, the user's request verbatim and the clarifications. It checks requirement coverage, risky assumptions, missing tasks and tests, task order and Definition-of-Done quality, and returns strict JSON findings.

notices.message: When a session starts in a repository, Buracle now links the skills in .agents/skills into .claude/skills so Claude Code sees them too, and checks that AGENTS.md lists the path rules in .claude/rules. Run `buracle project check` to see what it would change.

Buracle's CLI is smaller: run `buracle` in a terminal for a main menu you drive with the keyboard. `buracle install` now does what `init` and `sync` did, `buracle install` and `buracle update` apply in a terminal without a question and show each step as it runs, and the rare cases flags used to cover are questions in a terminal. `buracle help --all` lists the commands your agents use.
